title: Commercial discounts governance and approval matrix — guidance for forecasting, contracts, and billing
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines the governance, approval matrix, and required accounting and forecasting treatments for commercial discounts and one-off pricing concessions at Redwood Inference. It connects contract-level decisions to procurement and forecasting processes and prescribes the billing and revenue recognition (revrec) handling required to keep forecasts, SOWs, and GL entries consistent.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: provide a single-source policy for how discounts are requested, approved, documented, and reflected in forecasts and revenue recognition.
- Scope: applies to all customer-facing commercial discounts (list price reductions, promotional credits, implementation discounts, free-trial conversions, and market-development funds) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private offerings. Includes sales, customer success, finance, legal, and procurement interactions.

Definitions
- Net Price: list price less approved commercial discounts.
- One-off credit: single invoice credit applied for retention or remediation.
- Promotional credit: time-bound credit used for trial/POC conversions; typically expires after 90 days.
- Billing trigger: event that starts invoicing (e.g., contract signature, provisioned capacity, first API request).
- Revenue trigger: performance obligation satisfaction event for revrec determination.

Key principles
1) Separation of commercial and accounting approvals
   - Commercial teams (Sales/CS/Go-to-market) drive negotiation and propose discounting rationale.
   - Finance (Revenue Operations) validates accounting treatment and ensures revenue recognition integrity.
   - Legal ensures contract clauses align with approved commercial terms.
2) Forecast first, finalize later
   - All discount proposals that materially (>5% ARR impact or >$50k annual value) change forecasted net revenue must be entered in the Forecast Adjustment Log (FAL) before signature.
3) Short-lived credits must be instrumented
   - Promotional credits must include explicit expiration and usage caps in contract exhibits to prevent open-ended liabilities.

Approval matrix (quick reference)
- Discount type: Standard list discounts (up to 15%) -> Approver: Sales Manager (auto-approve in CPQ).
- Discount type: Strategic/renewal discounts (15%–30%) -> Approver: Head of Revenue + Finance (email approval recorded).
- Discount type: >30% or ACV > $250k with discount -> Approver: CRO + CFO + Legal sign-off required; requires documented business case in Deal Approval Portal.
- One-off credits for remediation < $25k -> Approver: CS Manager.
- One-off credits >= $25k -> Approver: CS Head + Finance.

Approval matrix (table - text format)
| Discount band | Decision owner | Required artefacts | Accounting owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0–15% | Sales Manager (CPQ) | Quote in CPQ | RevOps | Auto-approved via CPQ ruleset |
| 15–30% | Head of Revenue + Finance | Deal memo (Deal Portal) | RevOps | Requires forecast adjustment entry |
| >30% or ACV>$250k | CRO + CFO + Legal | Business case + Legal termed amendment | RevOps + Treasury | Requires executive record and SSO sign-off |

Request and documentation workflow (numbered SOP)
1. Sales rep opens Deal Approval Portal entry with: customer, list price, requested discount, term, ARR/ACV impact, suggested billing trigger, and proposed contract clause (if non-standard).
2. Generate CPQ quote draft, attach to Deal Approval Portal.
3. If discount triggers Finance review (per matrix), RevOps assigns a ticket; Sales cannot share final contract until RevOps approves forecast treatment.
4. Legal drafts amendment or exhibit; Finance signs off on the wording required for revrec (see Section: Contract language for revrec).
5. Once all approvals are captured, update Forecast Adjustment Log (FAL) with expected ARR impact and expected billing/recognition dates.
6. Procurement and Revenue Operations create billing schedule in Stripe/Billing system and set GL mapping.

Contract language guidance for revrec and billing triggers
- Always include: "Billing Trigger" and "Revenue Recognition Trigger" as discrete clauses. Example snippet: "Billing will commence on the later of (a) signature date or (b) provisioning of Dedicated capacity. Revenue will be recognized ratably over the contracted service term from the revenue trigger date unless otherwise specified per Section X."
- For promotional credits: include an exhibit specifying credit amount, expiration date, and applicability (applies to invoice # or product SKU).
- For multi-element deals (e.g., implementation + dedicated capacity + premium support), use explicit deliverable definitions and assign revenue allocation percentages in an attached Schedule.

Forecasting and GL mapping rules
- Short-term forecast adjustments: FAL entries are visible to FP&A and product finance. Add the following fields in the FAL entry: expected billing start, expected billing cadence, expected ARR delta, probability (sales stage), revrec method (ratable / milestone), GL accounts for deferred revenue and recognized revenue.
- GL mapping: standard SaaS mapping applies. Examples: 
  - Deferred Revenue: 2400
  - Subscription Revenue: 4001
  - One-off professional services: 4105
  - Promotional Credits (contra revenue): 4200
- Example calculation (promotional credit applied at signing):
  Example: Customer signs a 12-month Hosted plan at list $120,000 (monthly $10,000), promotional credit $12,000 applied at signing as invoice credit. Net invoice on month 1 = $0; months 2–12 = $10,000. Accounting: recognize subscription revenue ratably $120,000/12 = $10,000 per month; apply contra revenue entry for $12,000 recognized in month 1 as reduction of billed revenue and amortize the credit over same term if credit is to be applied pro rata (documented in contract). If credit is a one-time bill credit that only reduces invoice 1, record a contra-revenue of $12,000 in month 1 and adjust cash/AR accordingly. Consult RevOps on scenario.

Procurement interactions and templates
- Procurement is involved for integration/implementation discounts when a 3rd-party vendor or internal service must be purchased to fulfill the deal. Proc must:
  - Validate supplier onboarding (if vendor is required).
  - Confirm PO requirements and lead times in SOWs.
- Template checklist for procurement-triggered discounts:
  - SOW attached (Y/N)
  - External supplier required (Y/N) -> vendor name and onboarding status
  - Estimated vendor cost and margin impact
  - Payment terms to vendor vs customer terms alignment

Revenue recognition decision tree (short)
1. Is there a distinct performance obligation? -> Yes: allocate transaction price. No: treat as combined service.
2. Is discount contingent on future activity? -> Yes: treat as variable consideration; use expected value method and constrain estimates when necessary.
3. Is billing in arrears or in advance? -> Adjust timing of deferred revenue and invoicing entries accordingly.

Operational controls and required system changes
- CPQ must enforce discount bands and flag deals that require escalated approvals.
- Deal Approval Portal must capture all artifacts and approval audit trail.
- FAL must be integrated into forecasting model (monthly sync) and surfaced to FP&A with probability-weighted scenarios.
- Billing systems must support invoice credits and contra-revenue GL mapping; Stripe/Billing templates should be updated with new credit types: promo_credit, remediation_credit, reseller_margin_adjust.

Escalation and exceptions
- Exceptions to the approval matrix require an exception memo submitted to Finance with CRO/CFO signoff; exception memos are retained for audit for 7 years.
- Immediate remediation credits (customer incident) may be provisionally issued by CS up to $5k and must be logged in the Incident Credits Log within 48 hours; any credit > $5k requires Finance approval before issuance.

Audit and reporting
- Monthly reports: pipeline impact from approved discounts, realized discount rate (ACV-weighted), number of exception memos, and remaining deferred revenue attributable to credits.
- Quarterly audit: Internal Audit will sample 10 deals (> $50k) each quarter to confirm approval trails and GL treatment.

Appendices
A. Sample CPQ approval comment template
  - "Reason for discount: [strategic/renewal/retention]
  - Expected ACV impact: $[amount]
  - Forecast entry ID: FAL-[YYYY]-[NNNN]
  - Approvals captured: [names]"

B. Example phrasing for invoice credit exhibit
  - "Company will provide a promotional invoice credit in the amount of $X to be applied against the first invoice. The credit expires if not applied within 90 days of execution and is non-transferrable."

C. Quick checklist for RevOps before invoice issuance
- Confirm approved discount attached to CPQ quote.
- Verify FAL entry and expected billing cadence.
- Confirm GL coding for deferred revenue and contra entries.
- Ensure legal exhibit is attached to contract for promotional credits.
